meta.note: Maps characters containing the glyph 月 (directly or via immediate component) to its historical root node.

etymology_notes.朝: Often listed as Moon (日月) or Boat (舟); in oracle bone script (朝), the right side is actually 凡/舟 (river tide) or 月 (moon at dawn). Dual-tagging Moon + Time is standard for learners.
etymology_notes.有: Debated in paleography: traditionally 𠂇 (hand) + 肉 (meat), though sometimes taught mnemonically as hand eclipsing the moon.
etymology_notes.霸: Rain (雨) + leather (革) + moon (月, referring to the first phase of the lunar month 朏/魄).

舟_boat.gloss: boat; vessel (clerical script corruption of 舟)

etymology_notes.服: Left side is 舟 (boat); right side 𠬝 is a kneeling person (卩) controlled by a hand (又) — originally steering/subduing a boat.
etymology_notes.朕: Left side is 舟 (boat); right side originally 灷 (fire/caulking tool) — caulking the seams of a boat.
etymology_notes.前: Originally 歬: a foot (止, top) standing on a boat (舟, bottom left) moving forward without walking; knife (刂) added later.
etymology_notes.俞: Originally a hollowed-out canoe: Δ (集/𠓛) + 舟 (corrupted to 月) + 刂 (water current 巛 corrupted to knife).
etymology_notes.朝: Right side in Bronze script was 舟 (later conflated with 月) representing rising river tides at dawn.

etymology_notes.青: Top is 生 (sprouting plant) + bottom is 丹 (cinnabar mining pit/well), representing blue-green mineral pigment; bottom 丹 was stylized into 月 (or 円) during clerical transition.

etymology_notes.肯: Top 止 (bone/foot) + bottom 肉 (flesh attached to bone — the best cut of meat, hence 'willing').
etymology_notes.育: Top 𠫓 (upside-down newborn child 子) + bottom 肉 (flesh/afterbirth).
etymology_notes.肖: Small (小) + flesh (肉) — flesh of one's own flesh, hence 'resemble'.
etymology_notes.能: Pictograph of a bear: 厶 (head) + 肉 (body flesh) + 匕匕 (claws).
etymology_notes.然: Meat (肉/月) + dog (犬) + fire (灬) — roasting dog meat over fire.
etymology_notes.祭: Meat (肉/月) + hand (又) + altar (示) — hand offering meat on an altar.
etymology_notes.胡: Old (古) + flesh (肉) — originally the dewlap/neck wattle of an ox.
etymology_notes.散: Originally pounding meat (肉) or hemp with a stick (攵) under bamboo/forest (𥫗).

朋.note: Pictograph of two strings of cowrie shells/jade hanging side by side; unrelated to moon or flesh.

且.note: In 助, 阻, 租, 组, 粗, 祖, the component is 且 (U+4E14), not 月, though learners often confuse them visually.
